{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"“Don’t answer her,” her mother said. “She can only keep what you give her.”

The little girl laughed softly. Mara heard the sound from inside the stair and, a heartbeat later, from her own mouth. The boy backed away, lantern shaking in his hand.

Mara tried to say his name. She knew she had heard it that morning. Now she could remember only the shape of his face when he had told her.

The gap in her door widened. Beyond it, steps descended through black water. On the nearest step sat a child in a coat much too large for her, patiently wringing out its sleeves. Her face was hidden by wet hair.

“She gave me the name,” the child said. “I waited until you were old enough to share it.”

The dry door rang again. Two strikes. Mara looked at the clapper in her hand, then at the scratched letters on the iron. There were two strokes across the first letter, one newer than the other.

“Mother,” she called. “What was my name before?”

Silence. The child stood up. Water climbed the stair behind her, step by step.

“I never chose one,” her mother said at last. “The keeper said there wasn’t time.”

Mara put the clapper against the glass once more. The seventh wheel held still. With her free hand, she dragged a nail across the warm iron, cutting a line through the name.

The child cried out. The boy lifted the lantern higher so Mara could see where to make the next mark."}
